prerequisites: basic knowledge of secondary school mathematics

learning_outcomes.text: Acquaint students with the basics of linear algebra, vector calculus, analytic geometry and differential and integral calculus of functions of one variable, enabling them to attend engineering courses and deal with engineering problems.
Students will be made familiar with linear algebra, analytic geometry and differential and integral calculus of functions of one variable.
Students will be able to solve systems of linear equations and apply the methods of linear algebra and differential and integral calculus when dealing with engineering tasks.
After completing the course, students will be prepared for further study of technical disciplines.

syllabus_topics: Basics of mathematical logic and set operations
Matrices and determinants (transposing, adding, and multiplying matrices, common matrix types)
Determinants and their properties
Regular and singular matrices
Inverse to a matrix, calculating the inverse to a matrix using determinants
Systems of linear algebraic equations (Cramer's rule, Gauss elimination method)
Frobenius theorem
Calculating the inverse to a matrix using the elimination method
Vector calculus (operations with vectors, linear combinations and linear independence of vectors, scalar (dot) product, vector (cross) product, scalar triple (box) product)
Eigenvalues of a matrix
The notion of a function (domain and range, bounded functions, even and odd functions, periodic functions, monotonous functions, composite functions, one-to-one functions, inverse functions)

Basic elementary functions (exponential, logarithm, general power, trigonometric functions and cyclometric (inverse to trigonometric functions), polynomials (root of a polynomial, the fundamental theorem of algebra, multiplicity of a root, product breakdown of a polynomial), introducing the notion of a rational function)
Sequences and their limits
Limit of a function
Continuous functions
Derivative of a function (basic problem of differential calculus, notion of derivative, calculating derivatives, geometric applications of derivatives)
Calculating the limit of a function using L' Hospital rule
Monotonous functions, maxima and minima of functions, points of inflection, convex and concave functions, asymptotes, sketching the graph of a function
Differential of a function
Taylor polynomial
Parametric and polar definitions of curves and functions (parametric definition of a derivative, transforming parametric definitions into polar ones and vice versa)
Primitive function (antiderivative) (definition, properties and basic formulas)
Integrating by parts
Method of substitution
Calculating a primitive function by the method of substitution in some of the elementary functions
Riemann integral (basic problem of integral calculus, definition and properties of the Riemann integral)
Calculating the Riemann integral (Leibniz-Newton's formula)
Applications of the definite integral (mainly surface area of a plane figure, length of a curve, volume and lateral surface area of a rotational body)
Improper integral
Revision of knowledge gained at secondary school
Seminars related to the lectures given in the previous week
Elementary arithmetic
Calculations and evaluation of expressions
Solving equations
Finding roots of polynomials
Graph of a function of one real variable
Symbolic computations
assessment_rules: Students must achieve at least 6 points in each of the two seminar written tests to obtain course-unit credit. The exam has a written part (at most 75 points) and an oral part (at most 25 points). In the oral part, students must explain their solutions to the written test problems; failure to explain sufficiently will result in 0 points for the test. Final classification ranges from A (90-100 points) to F (0-49 points).
